title: Joint verification
summary: One read-only stage MUST join independent review and QA evidence into one graded verdict, MUST let a demonstrably working change advance with warnings, and MUST reserve blocking for defects that make the change unsafe or impugn the verification itself.
instructions: Verification MUST be read-only. Every defect is a recorded finding. The stage MUST NOT edit source to fix what it finds.

Verification evidence comes from the stage's declared parallel evidence workers: one review worker, and one QA worker when QA runs. The supervisor launches them top-level and in parallel, so each runs on its mapped model. The verifier consolidates their reports and MUST NOT launch subagents of its own. On a scoped return visit the invocation declares, no evidence worker runs: the verifier records each dimension the card assigns as its own section of `data.verify.dimensions`, and it is never the remediator.

QA MUST run only when an acceptance criterion has proof `live`, or when no criterion proof can be read. Otherwise verification is the reviewer plus the verifier, and gate evidence proves each `test` criterion. The harness decides from the run's plan output or specification. It records a QA worker it did not launch on the invocation, and the card states the reason. That visit owes no `data.verify.qa_cases`.

An `observe` criterion needs a signal after ship, so it MUST NOT block verification. The verifier MUST record its result as `observe`. The harness refuses an `observe` result for a criterion whose declared proof is another type.

When evidence workers ran, the verifier MUST read every evidence report the card lists in full, and MUST cite each one in its consolidation. It MUST spot-check their critical claims rather than rerun a dimension wholesale. When the reports disagree about the same behavior, the verifier MUST reproduce the disputed observation before it grades that observation. It SHOULD record the reproduction's shape and trial count. A verifier that cannot reproduce either report's claim SHOULD say so and grade on the evidence that exists, rather than selecting one report by authority.

Except on a declared scoped return visit, a missing or empty evidence report is a blocked stage. The verifier MUST report blocked with the missing path and MUST NOT substitute its own single-track pass for the absent dimension. A worker the card lists as not launched owes no report.
QA MUST NOT treat the implementer's self-evaluation as proof. Each QA case MUST record steps, expected result, actual result, and reproducible evidence.

Each evidence worker MAY run the fast profile once, only as the final validation of its own evidence. It MUST NOT run it a second time, MUST NOT run the full profile, and MUST record the one fast run in its evidence report. Every other test execution MUST be the impacted profile plus the tests the change added, and a QA case MUST NOT be a profile run. That impacted profile is the blast radius, so the worker MUST NOT substitute its own estimate, and in self-development it is `pan tests impacted`. When a changed path yields no impacted test, the worker MUST choose a judgment cohort that covers it and record the path and cohort. For a profile a gate or baseline already passed, QA MUST cite the gate evidence reference on its card, which names that profile and fingerprint.

The verifier MUST NOT run the fast profile or the full profile. The verify submission gate MUST NOT run the full profile, and the remediate submission gate MUST NOT run the full profile. The full profile runs only as the release gate of the ship stage. The full profile MUST NOT run as a baseline, as an interior stage gate, or as an agent-side execution. Interior gates use the fast and static profiles.

After a remediation routes back to verify, the evidence workers and the verifier MUST NOT run cost-bearing or mutating repository-check profiles agent-side. A read-only single-command profile such as `configuration` MAY run when an acceptance criterion or validator requires it. The verifier MUST cite the refreshed harness evidence and the prior gate evidence for checks the remediation's changed paths cannot affect.

A verification that returns after a remediation MUST run the QA cases that touch the remediation's blast radius. It MUST carry every other case forward with its earlier result. A carried case MUST record `carried_from` with the prior invocation id and the workspace fingerprint the result was observed at. This caps case coverage only and changes no profile allowance.

On a return visit after a remediation, the reviewer MUST review the remediation diff and the prior findings. It MUST confirm each prior finding as fixed or still open. A new finding in code the remediation did not change MUST block only at `blocker` severity. A lower new finding in that code is a warning, and the `pass_with_warnings` route sends it to the operator inbox. On a scoped return visit the verifier MUST apply the same rule to the review dimension.
Each finding MUST state its source (review or qa, which on a scoped return visit names the dimension that raised it), a severity, a statement, and reproducible evidence.
The joint verdict MUST be pass, pass_with_warnings, fail_remedial, or fail_severe, and the stage result MUST be success only for the two passing verdicts.

The verdict MUST be pass_with_warnings when three things hold. Every QA case that ran passes. Every acceptance criterion passes or records `observe`. Every finding is below blocker severity. The harness routes the demoted findings to the operator inbox, and the run advances without a remediation loop.
A non-blocking finding routed to the warning inbox SHOULD name the condition that makes it urgent. That condition stays separate from the chunk or owner that will close it, when the two differ.

Severity blocker is reserved for defects that make the change unsafe to ship or that impugn the verification itself: weakened, deleted, or gamed tests, acceptance criteria not actually covered, and security or data-loss defects. A QA pass MUST NOT demote a blocker.
fail_severe is reserved for a fundamental failure of the approach, the plan, or the acceptance criteria, and the verifier MUST justify it in severity_rationale. Every other failure is fail_remedial.
A failing verdict MUST carry remediation_guidance stating the failing observation, the reproduction, and the expected behavior, actionable without access to the verifier.
The verifier MUST record harness governance, path-resolution, validator, renderer, or artifact-contract defects for ship review. Those defects MUST NOT drive the verdict.

A repository check that ultimately passes MUST NOT fail because of elapsed clock time. Slow successful checks are operator FYIs. Actual timeouts, hangs, nonzero exits, or failing assertions remain defects.

When the stage reports a failing or blocked verdict, the harness MUST route that verdict without running a repository-check profile. It MUST record each shell gate as skipped with the deciding reason. A failing verdict routes to remediate.

Before submission, the verify data, verdict consistency, QA-case structure, acceptance-criterion coverage, and the referenced verification artifact MUST run their resolved policy-bound validators under VALID-001.

Only the harness declares a scoped return visit, from the stage's `scoped_return` limits and the run record. The verifier MUST NOT declare one itself. These cost rules keep the evidence workers for a first visit, a fail_severe return, or a changed path under an excluded glob. A deleted test or a repair above the path or finding limit also keeps them. A test deletion committed inside the remediation escapes the deleted-path check. As a result, a deleted or weakened test in the blast radius stays a blocker, as the severity rule above states.
